prompt:
In pipeline, does each new item wake many waiting threads, with all but one going straight back to sleep? If so, which threads, and what change would fix it?

Begin your answer with exactly one line: "Verdict: yes", "Verdict: no", or "Verdict: cannot tell from this trace". Then answer the question.
answer:
Verdict: no

## Wake-up pattern

Across the whole trace (0–30,902 ms), the parser (TID 644355) made 31,047 wake-ups, releasing an average of 1.9 threads per wake-up. Only 0.32% of wake-ups released three or more threads, and the finding classifies this as “wakes one thread at a time,” not a thundering herd. About 46.7% of the woken threads ran for under 0.05 ms before waiting again—likely finding no work.

The waiting threads woken by the parser were sink-0 (TID 644351), sink-1 (644352), sink-2 (644353), and sink-3 (644354). The trace does not say which individual sink threads made up the 46.7% that quickly waited again.

## Wait chain and impact

The parser ended 56.8% of other threads’ waits, but its impact is explicitly rated **negligible**: it was running 20.7% of the time and was itself mostly woken by the reader (TID 644356). For example, sink-0’s longest wait was 387.8 ms; it waited on the parser, whose progress depended mostly on the reader’s 387.3 ms timer wait.

So the trace does not show the proposed many-threads-per-item wake-up problem, and it does not point to a change needed to fix that problem.
